style: Black look (rule 19) with a mint accent: near-black, no frame or glow, one accent word, whole frame, calm. E30 wiggle family, try 1: three tabs; BEFORE every tap turns one tab bold (Open Sans 400 to 800, real measured widths) and the others jump sideways, ghost of the old place, TAPS / WIGGLES counted; AFTER every tab keeps a slot as wide as its bold copy and nothing moves

voice.text: Why do your tabs wiggle? The one you tap turns bold, and bold letters are wider. So it shoves its neighbours aside. The fix: hide a bold copy inside every tab. Now every tab is already wide enough, so nothing moves.

caption:
Why do your tabs wiggle when you tap them? 👆 You tap one, it turns bold, and every tab beside it jumps sideways.

Bold letters are wider than regular ones, so the bold tab needs more room and shoves its neighbours along. The fix: hide a bold copy of the label inside every tab, so each tab is always as wide as its bold self. Put the label in a data-text attribute too, then: .tab::after { content: attr(data-text); font-weight: 800; display: block; height: 0; visibility: hidden; } Make the tab an inline-block, and use the same weight as your active tab. Watch the reel: before, every tap is a wiggle; after the fix, the count stays at 0.

attr() inside content works in every browser, old ones too (MDN).

Save it for your next tab bar, or send it to whoever builds your UI.

sources.note: MDN attr() (page source mdn/content, read 24 Nov 2026): attr() retrieves the value of an attribute of the selected element; used with a pseudo-element it returns the attribute's value on the pseudo-element's originating element; MDN's own example is ::after { display: block; content: ... attr(cite) ... }
MDN BCD css.types.attr (read 24 Nov 2026): attr() with content since Chrome 2, Firefox 1, Safari 3.1, Edge 12

MDN ::after (page source, read 24 Nov 2026): creates a pseudo-element that is the last child of the selected element, used with the content property; it is inline by default (so the copy needs display: block to count as its own line)

tip.title: Why do your tabs wiggle when you tap them?
tip.why: The active tab turns bold, and bold letters are wider than regular ones, so the tab grows and pushes the tabs beside it sideways on every tap. Give every tab a hidden bold copy of its label: the tab is then always as wide as its bold self, and a tap moves nothing. The copy is an ::after pseudo-element that reads the label from a data-text attribute (MDN: attr() on a pseudo-element returns the attribute of its originating element). It has no height and is hidden, so nobody sees or hears it. attr() inside content works in every browser (MDN BCD: Chrome 2, Firefox 1, Safari 3.1).
tip.code:
<button class="tab" data-text="Following">Following</button>

.tab { display: inline-block; }
.tab::after {
  content: attr(data-text);
  font-weight: 800;   /* the active tab's weight */
  display: block;
  height: 0;
  visibility: hidden;
}
